c.v: Pittsfield Charter Township had 39,147 residents in the 2020 Census, up from 34,663 in 2010. It lies south and east of Ann Arbor, between the city, Ypsilanti, and Saline. I-94 crosses its north side, US-23 its east side, and Michigan Avenue (US-12) runs diagonally through its southern half.

Most township residents have an Ann Arbor, Ypsilanti, or Saline mailing address. Even the Township Hall, at 6201 W. Michigan Avenue, uses an Ann Arbor address. A crash or fall that seems to have happened “in Ann Arbor” may be a Pittsfield Township claim, and that changes who owns the road, which police agency wrote the report, and which court hears a small claim.

In 2024, the Michigan State Police recorded 1,143 crashes in the township. Of those, 215 injured someone and 3 were fatal. Four of Washtenaw County’s ten highest-crash intersections that year were in Pittsfield Township, three of them on Carpenter Road.

c.v: Carpenter runs north and south through the east side of the township. It passes big-box stores, shopping centers, apartment complexes, and bus stops, and it crosses Packard, Ellsworth, and Michigan Avenue. Three of the county’s ten highest-crash intersections in 2024 were on it, including the only one with a death.
In its 2026 request for state funds for a corridor study, the township described Carpenter Road this way:

items.v: one of the most dangerous roads in Washtenaw County for pedestrians, cyclists, and drivers
the site of multiple pedestrian deaths in 2025
among the highest traffic volumes in the county

c.v: A 2025 road safety audit of Carpenter and Packard found numerous risks to people on foot and on bikes. The Road Commission and the township have begun short-term changes such as pedestrian signal timing and new markings.
The typical crashes on Carpenter are:

items.v: left turns across several lanes
vehicles leaving parking lots
rear-end crashes at the signals
pedestrians crossing between signals to reach a bus stop or a store

c.v: Whether records from that audit can be used in a claim depends on how it was prepared and funded: federal law bars the use in court of safety data compiled for federally funded highway safety programs (23 USC 409), and later safety changes generally cannot be used to prove negligence (MRE 407). Washtenaw Avenue (M-17) is a multi-lane commercial road with driveways on both sides. Hogback Road at Washtenaw had 41 crashes in 2024, the third most in the county. The 14A-1 District Court sits on the same road. The common crashes are left turns, lane changes into an occupied lane (MCL 257.642(1)(a)), and drivers turning across a sidewalk into a business.

Michigan Avenue (US-12) runs southwest toward Saline past subdivisions, schools, and commercial strips. It meets Carpenter at the county’s eighth highest-crash intersection. State Street and Ann Arbor-Saline Road carry commuters into Ann Arbor past the I-94 interchanges. These are higher-speed roads, where the crashes are head-on and crossover crashes, left turns at unsignaled intersections, and crashes involving deer. In 2024, Washtenaw County had 1,409 deer crashes.

The two freeways meet at the township’s northeast corner. I-94 has interchanges at State Street and Ann Arbor-Saline Road, and US-23 at Michigan Avenue and Washtenaw Avenue. The crashes are rear-end, lane-change, and truck crashes, many of them in backups and construction zones. See our
The township has many apartment and condominium complexes, along with retail centers on Carpenter, Ellsworth, and Washtenaw. The recurring claims are:

items.v: falls on ice in parking lots and on walks
broken stairs and missing handrails
falls in stores
injuries from poorly lit common areas

c.v: A private landlord must keep the premises and common areas fit for their intended use and in reasonable repair (MCL 554.139). A lease clause waiving the landlord’s liability for its own negligence is void. A store owes customers reasonable care, subject to Michigan’s open-and-obvious doctrine, which since 2023 is weighed as part of comparative fault rather than as a bar. Injuries in township parks such as Lillie Park are limited by governmental immunity. See our

sections.heading: What is different about a Pittsfield Township claim

c.v: The township owns no roads, and who owns the road at the crash scene decides who you sue and how fast you must act.

items.v: Carpenter, Packard, Ellsworth, State Street, Platt, Hogback, and the subdivision streets belong to the Washtenaw County Road Commission. A claim against it for a road defect requires written notice within 120 days (MCL 691.1402, 691.1404).
I-94, US-23, US-12, and M-17 belong to MDOT. A road-defect claim against MDOT requires written notice filed with the Court of Claims within 120 days (MCL 691.1404).

the township has the duty for sidewalks along the roads, with its own 120-day notice (MCL 691.1401, 691.1402a, 691.1404). A sidewalk claim must also overcome a presumption that the township kept the sidewalk in reasonable repair, which a defect of less than two inches generally does not overcome.

c.v: Of the township’s four top-ten intersections, two are on state highways (Hogback at Washtenaw, and Carpenter at Michigan Avenue) and two are county-road intersections (Carpenter at Packard, and Carpenter at Ellsworth).
An Ann Arbor address is not an Ann Arbor claim.
A Pittsfield Township crash has these features:

items.v: The report is written by the township’s Department of Public Safety, not the Ann Arbor Police.
A small claim is filed in the 14A-1 District Court on Washtenaw Avenue, not the 15th District Court in Ann Arbor.
The road belongs to the Road Commission or MDOT, not the City of Ann Arbor.

c.v: The City of Ann Arbor’s crosswalk ordinance does not apply in the township. The state rules do: under the Michigan Uniform Traffic Code, which Pittsfield Township has adopted by reference, drivers must yield to a pedestrian in a crosswalk where there is no traffic signal. We confirm the jurisdiction from the crash report.

Your own household’s auto policy pays your medical bills and lost wages, whoever was at fault. A pedestrian or cyclist with no household policy is covered by the Michigan Assigned Claims Plan (MCL 500.3114, 500.3115, 500.3172). A claim against the at-fault driver for pain and suffering requires a serious impairment of body function, permanent serious disfigurement, or death (MCL 500.3135). It is reduced by your share of fault, and noneconomic damages are barred if you were more than 50% at fault (MCL 600.2959). The mini tort claim for vehicle damage is up to $3,000 (MCL 500.3135(3)(e)).
TheRide runs routes on Washtenaw Avenue, Carpenter Road, State Street, and Packard.

faqs.question: My address says Ann Arbor. How do I know if the crash was in Pittsfield Township?

answer.v: The crash report names the jurisdiction and the agency that responded. If it was the Pittsfield Township Department of Public Safety, the claim is a township claim. A mailing address does not settle it.

faqs.question: I was hit while crossing Carpenter Road. Who pays my medical bills?

answer.v: A no-fault policy in your household pays first. If there is none, the Michigan Assigned Claims Plan pays. Your claim against the driver for pain and suffering is separate, and the driver’s duty to yield is part of it.

faqs.question: Can I sue over a dangerous intersection?

answer.v: Sometimes. A road agency is liable only for failing to keep the roadway itself in reasonable repair, not for its design. The claim needs written notice within 120 days for a county road, or 120 days, filed with the Court of Claims, for a state highway.

faqs.question: I fell on a township sidewalk or pathway. Who is responsible?

answer.v: Usually the township, which has the sidewalk duty along the roads. Written notice is due within 120 days, and a defect of less than two inches is generally presumed not to be actionable.

faqs.question: Where would my Pittsfield Township case be filed?

answer.v: - Claims up to $25,000 go to the 14A-1 District Court at 4133 Washtenaw Avenue. - Larger injury suits go to the Washtenaw County Trial Court in Ann Arbor. - Claims against MDOT or the State go to the Court of Claims.
